analysis:
The PR changes only documentation in docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1561-1569). The added paragraph says LocalTokenizerBridge.decode in LocalTokenizerLoader.swift now releases a trailing run of <0xHH> byte-fallback tokens itself. A partial run reads as U+FFFD, which DetokenizerV2 holds back so segment restarts cannot land inside a character. No code is supplied, so the described behavior is unverified.

Security relevance is low. This is output-text correctness for Gemma 4 and does not touch encryption, attestation, authorization, key handling, the coordinator WebSocket contract (TB-002), or the cache storage and TTL posture (T-041). Decoded output is still encrypted per frame by ProviderLoop+InferenceHandler before it leaves the provider. The T-008 fail-closed behavior is not altered.

One possible side effect: forcing release of trailing bytes could change the timing or granularity of streamed chunks. T-041 covers the TTFT oracle, and this change does not alter the cache hit/miss signal, so I identified no new channel. The rest of the file (lines 1217-2026) is unchanged context with no security-relevant modifications, and I identified no regression.

Remaining integration question: the actual LocalTokenizerLoader.swift and DetokenizerV2 code is outside the evidence. It should be confirmed that a malformed or untrusted byte sequence cannot cause a crash or unbounded buffering, since the output text comes from model-generated tokens.
